# Linear Algebra and Multivariate Normal Toolkit {.appendix #sec-linalg-toolkit}

This appendix collects a small set of linear algebra definitions and identities that are used repeatedly in the multivariate normal, Gaussian processes, and optimization-based estimation. It is not intended to be exhaustive; the goal is to make later chapters locally self-contained.

## Vectors, Matrices, and Dimensions

Let $x \in \mathbb{R}^d$ be a column vector and let $A \in \mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ be a matrix. We write $A_{ij}$ for the $(i,j)$ entry and $I_d$ for the $d\times d$ identity matrix.

## Transpose

The transpose of $A$ is $A^\top \in \mathbb{R}^{n\times m}$ defined by $(A^\top)_{ij}=A_{ji}$. A matrix is symmetric if $A=A^\top$.

## Matrix-vector and Matrix-Matrix Multiplication

For $A \in \mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ and $x\in\mathbb{R}^n$, the product $Ax \in \mathbb{R}^m$ has entries $(Ax)_i=\sum_{j=1}^n A_{ij}x_j$.

For $A \in \mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ and $B\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times p}$, the product $AB\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times p}$ has entries $(AB)_{ik}=\sum_{j=1}^n A_{ij}B_{jk}$.

## Inner Product and Dot Product

For $x,y\in\mathbb{R}^d$, the standard inner product is
$$
\langle x,y\rangle = x^\top y = \sum_{i=1}^d x_i y_i.
$$

## Norms

The Euclidean (or $\ell_2$) norm is $\|x\|_2=\sqrt{x^\top x}$. More generally, for $p\ge 1$,
$$
\|x\|_p = \left(\sum_{i=1}^d |x_i|^p\right)^{1/p}.
$$
For a matrix $A$, a common norm is the Frobenius norm,
$$
\|A\|_F=\left(\sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n A_{ij}^2\right)^{1/2}.
$$

## Inverse and Matrix Inversion

For a square matrix $A\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}$, the inverse $A^{-1}$ satisfies $AA^{-1}=A^{-1}A=I_d$ (when it exists). A matrix is invertible if and only if its determinant is nonzero.

## Determinant

The determinant $|A|$ is a scalar associated with a square matrix. It is multiplicative: $|AB|=|A||B|$. For an invertible matrix, $|A^{-1}|=|A|^{-1}$.

## Trace

The trace of a square matrix is the sum of its diagonal entries:
$$
\operatorname{tr}(A)=\sum_{i=1}^d A_{ii}.
$$
It is invariant under cyclic permutations: $\operatorname{tr}(AB)=\operatorname{tr}(BA)$ whenever the products are defined.

## Positive Definiteness

A symmetric matrix $A\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}$ is positive definite (written $A\succ 0$) if
$$
x^\top A x > 0 \quad \text{for all } x\neq 0.
$$
It is positive semidefinite (written $A\succeq 0$) if $x^\top A x \ge 0$ for all $x$.

Covariance matrices are symmetric and positive semidefinite; in many models (e.g., multivariate normal densities) we require positive definiteness so that $A^{-1}$ exists and $|A|>0$.

## Eigenvalues and Eigenvectors

For a square matrix $A$, a nonzero vector $v$ is an eigenvector with eigenvalue $\lambda$ if $Av=\lambda v$. For symmetric $A$, eigenvalues are real and $A$ admits an orthonormal eigen-decomposition $A=Q\Lambda Q^\top$ with diagonal $\Lambda$.

## Singular Value Decomposition (SVD)

For any matrix $A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$, the SVD is
$$
A = UDV^\top,
$$
where $U\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times m}$ and $V\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ are orthogonal matrices and $D$ is diagonal (rectangular) with nonnegative singular values.

## A Key Quadratic Form Property (Gaussian Exponent)

Many Gaussian formulas reduce to manipulating quadratic forms of the type $(x-\mu)^\top\Sigma^{-1}(x-\mu)$. When completing the square, it is helpful to remember that for symmetric $\Sigma\succ 0$ and vectors $x,\mu$,
$$
(x-\mu)^\top\Sigma^{-1}(x-\mu)
$$
is always nonnegative and equals zero only when $x=\mu$.

## Marginals and Conditionals of a Multivariate Normal

Let $X\sim N(\mu,\Sigma)$ be a $d$-dimensional multivariate normal random vector with $\Sigma\succ 0$, and partition $X=(X_1,X_2)$ into blocks of dimensions $d_1$ and $d_2$ with $d_1+d_2=d$, so that
$$
\mu=\begin{pmatrix}\mu_1\\ \mu_2\end{pmatrix},\qquad \Sigma=\begin{pmatrix}\Sigma_{11}&\Sigma_{12}\\ \Sigma_{21}&\Sigma_{22}\end{pmatrix},\qquad \Sigma_{21}=\Sigma_{12}^\top.
$$
The marginal distribution of the first block is $X_1\sim N(\mu_1,\Sigma_{11})$, and its conditional distribution given the second block is normal,
$$
X_1\mid X_2=x_2 \sim N\left(\mu_1+\Sigma_{12}\Sigma_{22}^{-1}(x_2-\mu_2),\ \Sigma_{11}-\Sigma_{12}\Sigma_{22}^{-1}\Sigma_{21}\right).
$$
The conditional mean is affine in $x_2$ (linear plus a constant), and the conditional covariance does not depend on $x_2$. These are the identities behind the Gaussian process posterior in @sec-gp.
